scoringNote: Each property scored 0–2. Scores assigned based on static analysis of repository artifacts only. No implementations were guided by GS methodology.

implementations.label: Repo A — Community High Quality
implementations.communitySignal: ~2k GitHub stars; widely cited as NestJS reference implementation

self-describing.rationale: README present with installation steps, DB setup, NPM scripts, and Swagger API docs. No architecture doc, no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, no ADRs, no decision records. Layer structure is implicit via NestJS conventions, not documented.

bounded.rationale: NestJS module system enforces hard boundaries: article/, user/, profile/, tag/ modules each contain their own .module.ts, .controller.ts, .service.ts, .entity.ts. No cross-module leakage observed. Named modules with explicit responsibilities.

verifiable.rationale: 1 test file (tag.controller.spec.ts) with 1 it() assertion. Tests require a live MySQL connection (no mocking), making them non-executable without the DB. Effectively no coverage for any real business logic.

defended.rationale: No CI pipeline (.github/workflows absent, Travis badge dead). No active pre-commit hooks (only .git/hooks/*.sample files). No ESLint config. No commit convention enforcement.

auditable.rationale: Git log shows partial conventional commits: 'chore: update dependencies', 'chore(deps): bump...'. Many commits are non-conventional ('Update README.md', 'Replace crypto hashing with argon2'). No ADRs, no CHANGELOG.md, no decision records.

composable.rationale: NestJS DI via @Injectable + @InjectRepository(TypeORM Repository<Entity>). Constructor injection present. However, no custom repository interfaces (no IArticleRepository, IUserRepository). Services depend on TypeORM concrete generics. Modules cannot be swapped without TypeORM.

executable.rationale: README documents setup steps. tsc --noEmit passes after manual 'cp src/config.ts.example src/config.ts' step. Requires manually installing MySQL, creating database, configuring ormconfig.json. No docker-compose. Setup requires significant manual knowledge beyond what README provides.

externalToolResults.tscNote: 4 errors from missing config.ts (documented manual step). 0 errors after cp config.ts.example config.ts.
externalToolResults.installMethod: yarn install (npm install fails with 'Exit handler never called' — dependency resolution error)

implementations.label: Repo B — Official Reference
implementations.stack: Node/Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL + TypeScript + NX monorepo
implementations.communitySignal: Official gothinkster reference implementation; primary benchmark for RealWorld ecosystem

self-describing.rationale: README with clear setup steps (env vars documented, prisma commands, run command). Dockerfile present. No architecture doc, no CLAUDE.md, no ADRs, no layer descriptions beyond what code structure implies.

bounded.rationale: Feature routing subdirectories: src/app/routes/{article,auth,profile,tag}. Models in separate files. Controllers exist. BUT: services call prisma-client directly (no repository abstraction layer). No domain layer. Service and persistence concerns mixed.

verifiable.rationale: 6 test files, 27 it/test() calls, 18 describe blocks. Tests use jest-mock-extended to mock Prisma. Service tests cover error and success paths. Reasonable coverage of service logic but tests are mocked against implementations, not contracts. No integration tests.

defended.rationale: ESLint config present (.eslintrc.json) via @nx/typescript plugin. 33 ESLint violations in codebase (@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment, @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars) — not enforced as blocking gate. No CI pipeline (.github/workflows absent). No pre-commit hooks.

auditable.rationale: Recent commits follow conventional format ('fix: missing user id', 'chore: update documentation', 'chore: move to nx'). Older commits non-conventional. No ADRs, no CHANGELOG.md.

composable.rationale: Feature-based directory structure provides some module separation. No DI framework. Services import prisma-client directly (tight coupling to persistence). No repository interfaces. Modules are not independently swappable.

executable.rationale: README has clear setup steps. tsc --noEmit passes (0 errors). Dockerfile present (runtime only, not dev setup). No docker-compose. Requires external PostgreSQL with DATABASE_URL configured manually.

implementations.label: Repo C — GS-Generated (RX Output)
implementations.communitySignal: Experimental output — no community star count. RX run: 104/104 tests passing, 0 tsc errors, 0 CVEs.
implementations.scoringBasis: Generated code is gitignored. Scores inferred from: AX treatment evidence (RESULTS.md), RX build-log.txt, jest-output.json, run-metadata.json, and spec/conduit-gs.md.

self-describing.rationale: Per AX treatment evidence and RX spec: CLAUDE.md, Status.md, and README emitted as GS artifacts. JSDoc required on all public functions (lint gate). Layer boundary document embedded in spec and reflected in directory structure (src/api/, src/services/, src/domain/, src/ports/, src/adapters/).

bounded.rationale: Per AX treatment: 0 layer violations. Strict ports-and-adapters architecture with explicit src/ports/ directory for interface contracts. Composition root in index.ts. Services depend on port interfaces only. AX scored 2/2.

verifiable.rationale: RX evidence: 104 passing tests, 0 failures, 7 test suites (run-metadata.json). 80% line coverage gate enforced by spec. AX treatment: 143 it/test calls, 50 describe blocks. Tests against interfaces (not implementations) per port/adapter design.

defended.rationale: RX build-log.txt: 'found 0 vulnerabilities' on npm audit. No hardcoded secrets. ESLint configured per spec. HOWEVER: AX treatment and RX spec analysis show no CI pipeline (no .github/workflows). Pre-commit hooks specified in GS artifacts but AX showed they were not operationally enforced. Partial credit for 0-CVE npm audit and ESLint enforcement.

auditable.rationale: RX spec explicitly requires emitting ADRs as files: 'Emit each ADR as a file. An ADR that appears in a README as see ADR-0001 but does not exist as docs/adrs/ADR-0001-stack.md fails the Auditable gate.' ADR-0001 (Stack Selection) and ADR-0002 (SQL Injection Strategy) specified with full content. This is a stronger requirement than AX treatment, where ADRs were referenced but not emitted. Scored 2/2 on spec enforcement; noted with uncertainty since generated code is gitignored.

composable.rationale: Per AX treatment evidence: IUserRepository, IArticleRepository interfaces. Composition root in index.ts wires all dependencies. Services depend on abstractions. AX scored 2/2. Port/adapter pattern enforced by spec.

executable.rationale: RX run-metadata.json: numPassedTests=104, numFailedTests=0. build-log.txt: 0 tsc errors, 0 npm audit vulnerabilities. docker-compose.yml present in rx/ experiment dir. Prisma migrations run automatically. Passes the hard gate: tsc exits 0 AND jest numFailedTests === 0.

implementations.scoringDiscrepancy: Task prompt claims 14/14 from white paper. Evidence-based assessment yields 13/14 (Defended=1/2 due to absent CI pipeline, consistent with AX finding). The 14/14 claim likely reflects aspirational scoring of a fully-implemented CI gate that the AI-generated code specifies but does not physically provision.

externalToolResults.eslintNote: Per build-log.txt; ESLint in spec-required stack

finding: Rubric ranking (C > B > A) is congruent with external static analysis ranking on all three objective axes: CVE count, test count, and TypeScript health. The rubric captures nuances that star count misses: Repo A (2k stars) scores lower than Repo B (official reference) because community reputation tracks architectural elegance (NestJS framework discipline scores 2/2 on Bounded) but not test coverage (1 test case, 0/2 Verifiable) or security hygiene (105 CVEs including 16 critical, 0/2 Defended). The GS rubric is an orthogonal and more objective quality signal than star count.
